findings: In `summary.text`, change “traditionally associated with friendship” to identify friendship as an interpretation of the two-hand graph. The cited evidence supports proposed two-hands/friendliness analyses and a received Shuowen explanation, not an unqualified traditional association (X-c9abf151aed2704b4f9c, X-bd09127cafde84d80f20, X-bb0a75b2f367dc2fbc0f, X-0c27cb726a72d2f99696).

In `history[1].text`, replace “people who share aims and interact as friends” with the received explanation that people sharing aims are friends, and describe the graph as two 又 forms. The cited account does not say the forms depict people or that they interact (E3, E5, X-315eb525f264428e1a63, X-0df1a4c885bf11c3adb8).

In `components[0].text` and `learner.components[0].text`, cite evidence identifying 又 itself as a hand pictograph, and distinguish that origin from the proposed roles of the two 又 forms in 友. The current citations identify the repeated forms in 友 as hands but do not establish 又’s own pictographic origin; X-ce481aa81838231d5fbc supports the latter claim.
